claude.sample_unit: queries (15 open-ended questions and 25 simulated clinical scenarios)

links.outcome: Expert-graded accuracy of open-ended HCV answers with vs without guideline retrieval grounding
links.effect: Binary accuracy RAG-Top10 91.7% vs baseline 36.6% (p<0.001); RAG-Top1 81.7%; clarity 91.7% vs 46.6%.
links.quote: On open-ended questions, RAG-Top10 outperformed baseline in accuracy (91.7% vs. 36.6%; p < 0.001) and clarity (91.7% vs. 46.6%; p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Complete accuracy of DAA regimen recommendations in 25 simulated scenarios, RAG vs baseline
links.effect: Median accuracy baseline 24%, RAG-Top1 58%, RAG-Top10 76% (p<0.001 vs baseline).
links.quote: Similarly, RAG-Top10 achieved the highest performance in prescribing the correct DAA regimen according to expert consensus in 76% of cases (vs. 24% for baseline model, p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Baseline GPT-4 accuracy on guideline-based HCV knowledge and treatment selection
links.effect: Baseline binary accuracy 36.6% (guideline authors), 50% (tertiary experts); baseline correct DAA regimen in only 24% of scenarios.
links.quote: The baseline model demonstrated a median accuracy of 24.0% (IQR: 22%), the RAG-Top1 configuration showed marked improvement with a median accuracy of 58.0% (IQR: 10%, vs. baseline, p < 0.001), the RAG-Top10 configuration emerged as the superior performer, achieving a median accuracy of 76.0% (IQR: 8%, vs. baseline, p < 0.001) and the SFT model demonstrated a median accuracy of 66.0% (IQR: 19%, vs. baseline, p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Inter-grader agreement among blinded expert raters for accuracy and clarity
links.effect: Binary accuracy kappa slight to moderate (e.g., baseline 0.24-0.30); 10-point ICC higher (0.24 to 0.87); agreement varied by configuration and rater group.
links.quote: In addition, the use of binary metrics for evaluating accuracy and clarity resulted in a slight to fair agreement among graders, in contrast to using a point-based scale, which resulted in a higher agreement.

links.outcome: Effect of temperature/top-p settings and repeated runs on answer similarity to expert answers
links.effect: Optimal at temperature 0-0.8 and top-p 0-0.5; all models declined dramatically at temperature >=1.4 and top-p >=0.7; RAG-Top10 most robust.
links.quote: All models exhibit a dramatic performance decline with temperature ≥ 1.4 and Top‐ p ≥ 0.7, confirming that higher values introduce excessive variability in responses.

unlisted_practices: Comparing text chunking strategies (sentence, fixed-length, paragraph) and number of retrieved chunks for RAG
Supervised fine-tuning of an LLM on clinical guidelines and Q/A pairs

openai.sample_unit: distinct queries (15 open-ended questions and 25 simulated clinical scenarios)

links.effect: RAG-Top10 accuracy was 91.7% vs 36.6% baseline; RAG-Top1 81.7% and SFT 71.7%, p < 0.001.
links.quote: In binary accuracy grading, RAG‐Top10 showed the highest performance (91.7% accuracy), followed by RAG‐Top1 (81.7%) and SFT (71.7%), all significantly outperforming the baseline (36.6%, p < 0.001).

links.effect: RAG-Top10 median accuracy 76.0% (IQR 8%) vs baseline 24.0% (IQR 22%); RAG-Top1 58.0%, SFT 66.0%.
links.quote: The baseline model demonstrated a median accuracy of 24.0% (IQR: 22%), the RAG‐Top1 configuration showed marked improvement with a median accuracy of 58.0% (IQR: 10%, vs. baseline, p < 0.001), the RAG‐Top10 configuration emerged as the superior performer, achieving a median accuracy of 76.0% (IQR: 8%, vs. baseline, p < 0.001) and the SFT model demonstrated a median accuracy of 66.0% (IQR: 19%, vs. baseline, p < 0.001).

links.effect: Baseline median DAA-regimen accuracy was 24.0%; even RAG-Top10 reached 76.0%, leaving incorrect or incomplete recommendations.
links.quote: The baseline model demonstrated a median accuracy of 24.0% (IQR: 22%), the RAG‐Top1 configuration showed marked improvement with a median accuracy of 58.0% (IQR: 10%, vs. baseline, p < 0.001), the RAG‐Top10 configuration emerged as the superior performer, achieving a median accuracy of 76.0% (IQR: 8%, vs. baseline, p < 0.001) and the SFT model demonstrated a median accuracy of 66.0% (IQR: 19%, vs. baseline, p < 0.001).

links.effect: Performance declined dramatically at temperature ≥ 1.4 and Top-p ≥ 0.7, indicating excessive response variability.
links.quote: All models exhibit a dramatic performance decline with temperature ≥ 1.4 and Top‐ p ≥ 0.7, confirming that higher values introduce excessive variability in responses.

links.effect: Baseline clarity was 46.6%; RAG-Top10 91.7%, RAG-Top1 86.6%, and SFT 88.3%, all p < 0.001.
links.quote: Regarding clarity, RAG‐Top10 (91.7%), RAG‐Top1 (86.6%) and SFT (88.3%) all significantly outperformed the baseline (46.6%, p < 0.001).

links.quote: Both the RAG and SFT frameworks outperform the baseline model in terms of accuracy and clarity for questions related to HCV management.
